docs(console): describe the eight methods Console has, not the fourteen it doesn't (rich-docs-site-13t.4)

The ticket named `logLocals`. The page carried twenty-two false claims.

`Console`'s real surface is eight methods: print, log, rule, printJson,
beginCapture, endCapture, exportText, exportHtml. The page documented six
members that do not exist — `out`, `status`, `input`, `screen`, `pager`, and a
static `Console.capture()` — across five sections and two blocks that declared
`const console` twice, which would be a SyntaxError if run.

Three of those six are real capabilities documented on the wrong object. This
port moved several of Python Rich's Console methods to standalone classes, and
the docs were never told, so `status`, `input` and `screen` redirect to
`Status`, `Prompt` and `Live` rather than being deleted. `out` and `pager` have
no implementation anywhere and are gone.

The rest could not have been caught by any type checker, because every one of
them type-checks clean:

- `logLocals` is not configuration. `print()` sniffs its last argument for known
  option keys, so an unrecognized options object is demoted to a value to print,
  stringified to `[object Object]`, and eaten by the markup parser. It prints
  nothing — not, as the ticket assumed, a literal object.
- Printing or logging a plain object hits that same swallow and yields a blank
  line. The page claimed both were pretty-printed.
- `log()` adds a timestamp and nothing else; there is no location column.
- `rule()` does not parse markup in its title.
- `printJson` re-indents but does not colorize, while `print()` of the same
  string does.
- `crop`, `justify: "left"`, `justify: "full"` and `overflow: "ignore"` are
  accepted and inert.
- `NO_COLOR` strips bold along with colour, contradicting the page.
- The colour-system table listed two specs that throw, omitted the two that
  work, and gave the Windows palette as 8 colours where it has 16.

Every claim above was verified by executing it against a width-pinned console
and capturing stdout, and every code block on the page now type-checks against
`src/`.

Filed rather than fixed here: rich-console-nac (four inert PrintOptions),
rich-console-8lg (printJson's sortKeys silently no-ops via a cast to the
replacer parameter, and its missing highlighting), rich-docs-site-dl4
(docs/live.md documents `screen:`/`live.run()`/`new Table("a","b")`, none of
which exist — and console.md now links there).

docs(pretty): describe the Pretty renderable that exists, not the repr protocol that doesn't (rich-docs-site-13t.3) (#83)

* docs(pretty): describe the Pretty renderable that exists, not the repr protocol that doesn't (rich-docs-site-13t.3)

The ticket named the `richReprAuto` decorator. Grepping `richRepr` across `src/`
returns nothing — and neither do `rich.angular` or any other repr hook, so the
whole "Custom object representation" section was fiction, not just its last
subsection. It is deleted. Per the epic's direction, no repr protocol was
implemented to make the page true; the code is the truth and the page moves.

Deleting it left a page whose remaining claims were also false, and the premise
was the worst of them. The page opened with "`print()` and `log()` automatically
format containers." They do not. `Console.print` renders any non-renderable
through `String()` (src/core/console.ts, the `else` branch of the item loop), so
a plain object becomes the literal text `[object Object]` — which `renderMarkup`
then parses as a style tag and consumes. Printing an object prints a blank line.
`Pretty` is never reached unless you construct it. Every section is rewritten
around that.

Four sections then documented options that do not exist where they were shown.
`console.print(data, { indentGuides: false })` does not configure anything:
`PrintOptions` recognises only `style|justify|markup|highlight|overflow|end|
softWrap|crop|sep`, so the options object falls through as a second *value* to
print and disappears the same way. The options belong to `Pretty`'s constructor,
and the page now says so with the failing form shown beside the working one.

Both output blocks were fabricated, in four ways each: `│` indent-guide glyphs
(the guide is a `dim green` *space* — `Style.parse("repr.indent")`, applied by
`_addIndentGuides` to one space per level), two-space indents (the default is 4),
Python `'single'`-quoted keys and strings (keys print unquoted, strings via
`JSON.stringify`), and Python `True`. The `maxString` block claimed
`'…' +240 chars`; the real suffix is `+240` inside the quotes, as part of the
string. Every output block on the page is now captured stdout at width 43, and
the width is stated in the lead because it decides compact-vs-expanded.

New, and true: a class instance formats as a plain object from its own enumerable
properties, with no class name — which is the honest replacement for the section
that promised a repr hook. `Map` and `Set` have no one-line form. The compact-fit
test measures a container without the key it sits under, so a nested container
can overrun by the length of its key (filed separately).

Verified by extracting all nine ```typescript blocks verbatim, writing each to
its own file, rewriting the `@promptctl/rich-js` specifier to `src/index.js`, and
running `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` plus vitest over all nine. Per-file
isolation is what proves each block carries its own imports and `Console`. Gates:
`npm run lint` and `npm run docs:build` clean, `npm run test` 2113 passing.

* docs(pretty): pin the width the examples were captured at, and stop overclaiming maxLength

Review caught that the page named a console width of 43 while every snippet
constructed a bare `new Console()`. The default is 80 (console.ts:196, `w || 80`),
so a reader copying the first example got the compact one-line form where the page
showed the expanded one. Every snippet now passes `{ width: 43 }`.

The cause is worth naming because it is the same one review caught twice on #82:
I verified in a configuration that did not share the assumption under test. My
harness rewrote `new Console()` into `new Console({ width: 43, record: true })` so
it could capture output — and that rewrite is exactly what made the outputs true
in the harness and false on the page, the way `as never` did for the generator
claim last time. The blocks are now re-extracted with the `@promptctl/rich-js`
specifier as the only edit, and stdout is captured by swapping
`process.stdout.write` rather than by constructing a different Console.

`maxLength` was also described as if it annotated every container. It does not:
the array and plain-object branches compute `remaining` and append `... +N`, and
the `Map` and `Set` branches slice and stop. `new Pretty(map, { maxLength: 2 })`
drops entries with no marker at all, which is the opposite of what the sentence
promised. The claim is now split by what the code does, and the silent case is
stated as its own fact — a reader capping a large Map has no other way to learn
it. Filed onto rich-pretty-efq, which already carries the sibling `maxString`
annotation defect, so both land in one fix.

Verified: all nine blocks extracted verbatim, each to its own file,
`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` plus vitest, every output block diffed
against real stdout — including `"\nafter\n"` for the blank-line example.
Gates: `npm run lint` and `npm run docs:build` clean.

* docs(pretty): make every output block byte-exact, including the whitespace nobody can see

Review caught that the stray-options example omitted a real trailing space. The
item loop in `Console.print` pushes `new RichText(sep, { end: "" })` before every
item after the first, unconditionally and before it knows what that item renders
to — so the separator is written even though the options object renders to
nothing. Real stdout is `"[1, 2, 3] \n"`.

That was imprecise under the old lead and false under the new one: the previous
commit tightened the promise to "the output under it is that snippet's stdout,"
which retroactively turned a rounding-off into a lie. The space is now in the
block, and a sentence names it — an invisible character communicates nothing on
its own, and the separator is the fact the section is about.

Checking that claim properly then found the same class of error in the panel
example, which dropped the blank line a printed `Panel` always leaves: `Panel`
renders its own closing line break and `print` appends `end` regardless
(console.ts, where the comment explains the append must go through
`_writeSegments` or `exportText` would join consecutive prints onto one line).
Shown, and named.

The verification is now the thing that found these rather than the thing that
missed them. The harness pairs each ```typescript block with the fenced block
below it and asserts `stdout === block + "\n"` — byte for byte, whitespace
included — and the extractor asserts structurally that every code block pins
`width: 43` and has an output block, so a future block that forgets either fails
extraction instead of passing quietly. Eyeballing a diff is what let a trailing
space through twice.

All nine blocks pass. Gates: `npm run lint` and `npm run docs:build` clean.
